title: How many tiny squares are in the picture, and what are their primes?
description: The tiles are counted, then the tiny squares in one tile, and the two counts are multiplied. The total is written as primes and the primes are paired, which shows a square. Forty five times forty five puts the answer back.
teaching_notes: One idea: count in two steps, then pair the primes to see the square. Watch for students who count only the tiles, or who stop after multiplying and never write the primes.

video_script.why: The child counts the tiny squares in a tiled picture and uses the pairing of primes from the solved example to see that the total is a square.
video_script.substitution: Count the tiles, count the tiny squares in one tile, multiply, and write the total as primes.
video_script.anchor: a picture of nine rows of tiles with nine tiles in each row, every tile a five by five grid of tiny squares
video_script.payoff_line: There are two thousand twenty five tiny squares

final_answer.spoken: there are two thousand twenty five tiny squares, and its primes are four threes and two fives, which is forty five squared

video_script.design: One idea: count in two steps, then pair the primes. The picture stays in the anchor band and the counting lines sit on the working board.
open_questions: The book text does not describe the picture. Nine rows of nine tiles, each a five by five grid, comes from the worklist. Check it against the printed figure.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of tiny squares, and its prime factorisation

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of tiny squares, and write it as primes.

marks.tiles: 9 × 9 = 81 is written next to the nine rows

narration: <bookmark mark='tiles'/>Step one, count the tiles.
Nine rows of nine tiles make nine times nine, which is eighty one tiles.

marks.tiny: 5 × 5 = 25 is written next to one tile

narration: <bookmark mark='tiny'/>Step two, count the tiny squares in one tile.
Five rows of five make twenty five tiny squares.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Step three, multiply the two counts.
Eighty one tiles with twenty five tiny squares each give two thousand twenty five tiny squares.

beats.on_screen: prime factorisation of 2025: 2025 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5; all the primes join in pairs
narration: <bookmark mark='pf'/>Step four, use prime factorisation on two thousand twenty five.
It is four threes and two fives.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>All the primes make pairs, so this number is a perfect square.

beats.on_screen: put the answer back: (3 × 3 × 5) = 45 tiny squares along each side, and 45 × 45 = 2025

marks.group: one group of the paired primes is lifted out and 3 × 3 × 5 = 45 is written
marks.back: 45 × 45 = 2025 is written and ticked, and the picture is shown as 45 tiny squares each way

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question.
One group of primes is three times three times five, which is forty five.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Nine tiles of five make forty five tiny squares along each side. Forty five times forty five is two thousand twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>There are two thousand twenty five tiny squares.
Its primes are four threes and two fives, which is forty five squared.
